NIGHT BUS · SIDES · SHOOT DAY 1 · Second Draft
1. EXT. RAYAPURAM BUS STAND - DAY
A stray dog trots after the bus, then gives up at the bridge.
FADE IN:
Heat shimmer over a row of parked buses. Hawkers call out prices. A loudspeaker announces departures nobody can understand.
A green and cream bus, number plate RYP 0417, swings into the last bay. Painted on its side: RAYAPURAM TO PEDDA REVU, ALL STOPS.
FAROOQ (40s, driver, moustache, sleeves rolled) kills the engine and slaps the steering wheel like a horse's neck.
FAROOQ
Shabash. Two hundred kilometres and not one complaint.
The door hisses open. LAKSHMI (17, backpack, earbuds, a toolkit roll under one arm) steps down and squints at the town.
FAROOQ (CONT'D)
(calling after her)
Hey, engineer! You forgot your umbrella.
He tosses it. She catches it without looking.
LAKSHMI
It hasn't rained here in forty days.
FAROOQ
That is exactly when it rains.
2. INT. VENKAT RADIO WORKS - DAY
A narrow shop crowded floor to ceiling with radios: valve sets, transistor sets, a ship's receiver the size of a fridge. A ceiling fan turns slowly enough to count.
VENKAT RAO (70s, thick glasses on a string, cotton vest) bends over a workbench, SOLDERING IRON in hand. A thin curl of smoke rises.
Lakshmi stands in the doorway. He does not look up.
VENKAT RAO
If you are a customer, the shop is closed. If you are my granddaughter, you are late.
LAKSHMI
The bus was late.
VENKAT RAO
Farooq's bus is never late. It is only slow.
She drops her bag and hugs him from behind. He keeps soldering.
LAKSHMI
తాతయ్యా, you still have the fridge radio.
VENKAT RAO
It is a marine receiver. Show some respect.
He sets the iron in its stand and finally looks at her.
VENKAT RAO (CONT'D)
You grew. Did they teach you anything at that college?
LAKSHMI
Signals and systems. Mostly systems.
VENKAT RAO
Then you can hold this.
He hands her a MULTIMETER and points at two terminals.
3. EXT. VENKAT RADIO WORKS - ROOFTOP - DUSK
The town spreads out in orange light. A rusted ANTENNA MAST leans against the water tank, guy wires slack.
Wind rattles the antenna. Somewhere below, a radio plays an old film song.
Lakshmi climbs onto the parapet. Venkat Rao stays by the stairs, holding a cup of tea.
VENKAT RAO
Come down. That mast is older than your mother.
LAKSHMI
Why is it still up here?
VENKAT RAO
Because nobody asked me to take it down.
She runs a hand along a guy wire. It sings faintly in the breeze.
Source: THE TOWER AT PEDDA REVU: Second Draft
